“Ow… Once Saber agrees to do something, she really doesn’t hold back…”

I crawl beneath the covers.

My bruised body is plastered with medicated compresses. Tomorrow, muscle pain will join the assault.

My consciousness drifts in a haze.

My body remains asleep, unable to move so much as a finger.

pages.en:
Cold.

The wind cuts into my cheeks. My body, exposed to the night in nothing but sleeping clothes, has long since frozen through.

…It is a cold that does not belong in Fuyuki.

If this were a dream, the chill should already have shocked me awake.

…This coldness is unlike Fuyuki City.
The chill would be cold enough to wake me up if this were a dream.

Ignoring the body shuddering from the cold, my feet carry me toward some unknown destination.

It cannot be a dream.

My limbs refuse to obey me—Shirou Emiya—and walk onward as though controlled by invisible strings.

Turn back.

Turn back.

Turn back.

Stop your feet. There is still time. Turn back. Wake up and turn back now. Wake up. Wake up. Wake up. Whatever you do, do not listen to that voice…………!!!!

The fog clears from my mind, and at last my will returns to me.

Magi possess a natural resistance to magecraft.

It allows them to repel spells that constrain their actions—hypnosis, binding, compulsion, and the like.

So long as a person is a mage, another practitioner cannot control them with any ordinary spell.

As long as one is a magus, one cannot be easily controlled by others.

“Precisely. First I will peel away the skin, and then transplant the Command Spells to my Master.

“But the Command Spells are integrated with their owner’s Magic Circuits, are they not? To deprive you of them, I must also draw the Magic Circuits—the nerves themselves—from your body.”

Caster speaks lightly, as though describing nothing of consequence.

Caster says so as if it’s nothing at all.
